questions.question: What is the main value of keeping retrieval-level and generation-level metrics on separate ledgers?
options: It makes the evaluation run faster
Attribution: the demo's first round shows retrieval 0.7 against generation 0.8, so the weak leg immediately shows as retrieval
It lets you skip the golden dataset
It lets MRR replace the relevance metric
questions.explanation: See the "Two levels, two ledgers" section: keeping two ledgers is what makes attribution possible — the demo's first round shows retrieval 0.7 against generation 0.8, and the weak leg immediately shows as retrieval.

questions.question: In the demo, question 6's answer produces "shipping is free" even though no recalled chunk contains it. By R05's definition, what kind of error is this?
options: Hallucination — saying more than the sources say
questions.explanation: See the "Faithfulness: hallucination defined for RAG" section: this is hallucination's precise definition in the RAG context — saying more than the sources say.

questions.question: Why can the climb from 0.7 to 0.9 in the two-round demo be confidently attributed to chunking?
options: Because the temperature was also lowered
Because only the chunking strategy changed, nothing else, in a full re-run two-round comparison
Because the number of evaluation questions increased
Because a stronger embedding model was swapped in
questions.explanation: See the "Iteration with control: the 0.7 to 0.9 chain of attribution" section: the second round changes only the chunking strategy and nothing else — single-variable changes, full re-runs, two-round comparisons — so the gain can be confidently attributed to chunking.
